claims.claim_text_verbatim: We propose Residual Advantage (RA), which treats the teacher–student probability residual as a bounded one-step reward, subtracts the corresponding state value under the student policy to form a standard advantage, and centers the result within each response before adding it to the verifier advantage.
claims.claim_summary: RA treats probability residuals as bounded rewards, centering advantages before adding verifier feedback

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The guidance term has zero mean within each response, so the verifier advantage remains the response’s mean label and the teacher only redistributes credit among the steps within it.
claims.claim_summary: Zero-mean guidance preserves the response mean label while redistributing step-level credit

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Co-RA further updates a teacher LoRA with verifier advantages on the same scored student batch and uses the updated teacher in the next iteration’s residual, adapting guidance to the student’s attempts.
claims.claim_summary: Co-RA updates a teacher LoRA with verifier advantages to adapt guidance iteratively

claims.claim_text_verbatim: With Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base students and a Qwen3-8B teacher, RA combined with GRPO or REINFORCE++ improves the underlying sequence-advantage algorithm in all 24 comparisons on three mathematical benchmarks, raising macro Avg@8 by 1.7–3.6 points and Pass@8 by 3.9–6.3 points.
claims.claim_summary: RA improves underlying algorithms across 24 comparisons, boosting Avg@8 and Pass@8

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Both combinations surpass teacher-only OPD, and Co-RA adds a further 1.0–1.5 Avg@8 points.
claims.claim_summary: RA combinations beat teacher-only OPD, with Co-RA providing additional Avg@8 gains

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The guidance is thus student-relative twice over, as an advantage under the student’s own next-token distribution and as a deviation within the student’s own response.
claims.claim_summary: Guidance is student-relative via next-token distributions and internal response deviations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The construction requires no schedule, threshold, or learned component.
claims.claim_summary: The RA construction operates without needing schedules, thresholds, or extra learned parameters

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Training on the student’s own rollouts with the verifier’s advantages lets the teacher adapt to the reasoning along the student’s solution paths, with the aim of reducing the bias a frozen teacher carries on trajectories it would not have generated itself.
claims.claim_summary: Training teacher LoRA on student rollouts reduces frozen teacher trajectory bias

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across two students, two estimators, and three mathematical benchmarks, RA improves all 24 three-seed benchmark means of its base estimator, both combinations surpass teacher-only OPD, and Co-RA raises accuracy further with mixed changes in coverage.
claims.claim_summary: RA improves all base estimator benchmark means, beating OPD and raising accuracy

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The local advantage vanishes on a token the student has settled, whatever the teacher says, and by part (ii) logit b moves in expectation by p(b)(1 − p(b)) times a bounded contrast, so the teacher acts most where the student is undecided.
claims.claim_summary: Local guidance vanishes on settled tokens and acts primarily on undecided student choices

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The second bounds the guidance amplitude by the student–teacher distance on the visited prefixes (Appendix A.6), so teacher guidance fades as the two converge, at a fixed weight and without a schedule; Appendix C.1 shows the mean absolute guidance declining over a training run.
claims.claim_summary: Guidance amplitude is bounded by student-teacher distance, declining naturally as policies converge

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 1 contains 24 comparisons of RA with its base estimator (two students, two estimators, three benchmarks, two metrics), and RA improves all 24 three-seed benchmark means.
claims.claim_summary: RA outperforms base estimators in all 24 tested benchmark evaluation comparisons

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The macro gains are 1.74–3.58 Avg@8 and 3.89–6.33 Pass@8 points (Table 10).
claims.claim_summary: RA yields macro gains of 1.74-3.58 Avg@8 and 3.89-6.33 Pass@8 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The gains are larger for REINFORCE++, narrowing its macro Avg@8 deficit to GRPO at both sizes.
claims.claim_summary: REINFORCE++ sees larger gains with RA, narrowing its accuracy deficit to GRPO

claims.claim_text_verbatim: GRPO keeps the higher completion accuracy after guidance, but REINFORCE++ with RA has the higher macro Pass@8 at both sizes, a trade between accuracy and coverage that a single score would hide.
claims.claim_summary: REINFORCE++ with RA achieves higher Pass@8 coverage while GRPO retains higher accuracy

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Both RA combinations exceed teacher-only OPD in macro Avg@8 and Pass@8 at both sizes, by 1.80–2.96 and 2.73–3.90 points (Table 10).
claims.claim_summary: RA combinations outperform teacher-only OPD across both sizes in Avg@8 and Pass@8

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In training, OPD also starts more slowly than REINFORCE++ and stays below RA+REINFORCE++ over most of the shared budget (Appendix C).
claims.claim_summary: OPD learns slower than REINFORCE++ and trails RA+REINFORCE++ across most training

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At the same budget, OPD followed by REINFORCE++ reaches 28.39 and REINFORCE++ with an added reverse-KL loss 26.14, both below RA+REINFORCE++ (Appendix D.5), and sampling the log ratio at the generated token, with the same expected update at each prefix, drops OPD to 24.80 at 1.7B, below verifier-only training (Appendix D.6).
claims.claim_summary: Sequential OPD-then-RL and joint reverse-KL baselines perform below RA+REINFORCE++

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Co-RA adds 1.03–1.45 macro Avg@8 points to the four RA runs, and Avg@8 rises in all twelve benchmark means.
claims.claim_summary: Co-RA provides 1.03-1.45 additional Avg@8 points across all tested benchmark settings

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Co-RA+GRPO is the most accurate run for both students.
claims.claim_summary: Co-RA combined with GRPO achieves the highest accuracy across tested student models

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Yet each adapted teacher scores 0.8–2.3 macro Avg@8 and 0.7–3.5 Pass@8 points below the frozen teacher (Appendix D.9), while the students it guides improve: it is a better guide, not a better solver.
claims.claim_summary: Adapted teachers perform worse independently but act as superior guides for student models

claims.claim_text_verbatim: From K = 8 to K = 512 for the 1.7B REINFORCE++ runs (Appendix D.7), the macro margin of RA over the untrained student grows from 13.4 to 16.9 points, and its margins over REINFORCE++ and OPD from 5.8 to 10.4 and from 3.9 to 6.8, while that of verifier-only training narrows from 7.6 to 6.6, as Yue et al. (2025) report for RLVR.
claims.claim_summary: RA's performance margin over baselines expands significantly as sampling increases to K=512

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Removing the student value baseline lowers both macro scores, by 2.09 Avg@8 and 3.58 Pass@8 points at the reference weight and similarly at weights 5 and 20 (Table 2).
claims.claim_summary: Omitting the student value baseline reduces Avg@8 by 2.09 and Pass@8 by 3.58

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Removing both operations costs 1.73 Avg@8 and 2.77 Pass@8 points; the state value then also enters the response mean, shifting it by −0.32 on average and beyond 0.5 on a quarter of the offline responses (Table 16).
claims.claim_summary: Removing both baselines degrades performance and significantly shifts response label means

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Restoring response centering at the same weight adds 0.54 Avg@8 and 0.46 Pass@8 points, a smaller gain that holds at all three weights (Table 2).
claims.claim_summary: Response centering provides consistent gains of 0.54 Avg@8 and 0.46 Pass@8 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across seeds, full RA also varies less than the uncentered control in macro Avg@8 at every weight (Table 23).
claims.claim_summary: Full RA demonstrates lower variance across seeds compared to uncentered controls

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All tested weights improve both macro scores over verifier-only training (Table 2).
claims.claim_summary: Every evaluated RA weight setting improves scores compared to verifier-only training

claims.claim_text_verbatim: With both operations, clipped to [−5, 5] or not, the log ratio stays above verifier-only training at every swept weight, and the probability residual is better still, by 1.21 Avg@8 and 1.70 Pass@8 points over the best log variant.
claims.claim_summary: Probability residuals outperform the best centered log-ratio variants by over 1.2 Avg@8

claims.claim_text_verbatim: A full-vocabulary squared-distance loss, whose gradient at each visited prefix equals the expected update of the uncentered residual label (Appendix A.2), beats verifier-only training but stays below RA and the uncentered control at every weight (Table 2).
claims.claim_summary: Direct auxiliary L2 loss beats verifier-only baseline but performs below RA

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Because RA’s teacher term acts on the tokens the verifier scores, 64% of its gradient mass raises correct or lowers incorrect responses, against 49% for the direct loss, and after clipping and Adam the teacher takes 0.28 of the update against 0.44, keeping RA’s update closer to the verifier’s direction (cosine 0.93 against 0.80).
claims.claim_summary: RA's updates align more closely with verifier directions than direct loss updates

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The residual puts 59% of its guidance on the 12% of tokens with 0.1 ≤ p(at) < 0.5, five times their share, where the student is choosing among live alternatives.
claims.claim_summary: Residual guidance heavily concentrates on high-uncertainty decision tokens where probabilities are balanced

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The centered log ratio puts 50% of its total on the 4% of tokens the teacher assigns less than 10−4, where its label diverges.
claims.claim_summary: Centered log ratio allocates half its guidance to rare teacher tokens due to divergence

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under sampled OPD (Table 4) the branch raises macro Avg@8 from 24.80 to 25.10 and the Avg@8 of every seed.
claims.claim_summary: Adding a teacher-peak branch slightly improves sampled OPD performance across seeds

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under REINFORCE++, where λ scales only the branch, it lowers macro Avg@8 by 0.38–1.76 points and Pass@8 by 0.46–2.11 points, a loss that grows with the branch weight.
claims.claim_summary: Teacher-peak branch degrades REINFORCE++ performance proportionally to the branch weight

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Added to RA, it lowers macro Avg@8 by 2.05–2.16 points and Pass@8 by 3.41–3.91 points, and at every weight each seed falls below the same seed of RA, whereas doubling RA’s own weight does not (Table 2).
claims.claim_summary: Adding dense teacher-peak supervision to RA consistently reduces accuracy and coverage

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The guidance term decreases both as the student approaches the teacher and as the student becomes confident in its own choice, an elegant property that helps RA preserve exploration in RL.
claims.claim_summary: RA guidance automatically diminishes with student confidence or policy convergence, preserving exploration

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Up to Pass@512 the margin of RA over the untrained student grows while that of verifier-only training narrows.
claims.claim_summary: RA's advantage over untrained models expands with high sample counts, unlike verifier-only RL
